fields.System.Title: FDN-3 — Identity and permissions
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Every action in the system is attributable to a person or a machine, and only to someone
allowed to take it.

Scope

In. Users, login and tokens, roles and permissions, API clients for machine callers, user
deactivation.

Out. Single sign-on, LDAP, multi-factor authentication. Add when a real deployment demands
them.

Design notes

Build this before any business endpoint. Retrofitting "who did this?" into twenty existing
writes means touching all twenty and missing one — and the one you miss is the write that
matters during an investigation.

Permission checks belong in the API layer, before any service is called. Scattering them
inside services means some path eventually skips them.

Roles map to the warehouse, not to the software. Receiving clerk, picker, packer, inventory
controller, supervisor. See [doc 01 §3](../../../docs/01-product-overview.md) for what each may
and may not do.

Deactivate, never delete. A user's ID appears on years of movement rows.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Permission checks scattered so one endpoint is missed | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
| Anonymous writes possible on some path | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
| Deleting a user orphans historical movements | [doc 03 §5](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
